scope_limits: The PDP is this repository's gateway-authz, built with the `acceptance` tag: the product code plus the test controls this runner uses (request log, fault modes, revoke/restore). The product build, which has none of them, is not what ran. Where a case says "Gatekeeper" or "PDP" it means this process.

gateway-authz reads its policy and its credentials from files written for the run and keeps revocations in memory. No identity provider, grants store, Secret Manager or provider token endpoint is involved, and the deployed Gatekeeper is not called: the caller tokens are signed by a key made for the run.
The provider is a loopback mock; no carrier sandbox was called.

Mutual TLS is real on the gateway-to-PDP and broker-to-PDP hops only, with a CA and certificates made for the run: no SPIFFE Workload API, no rotation, no certificate revocation. Caller-to-gateway and gateway-to-provider are plain HTTP.

The local broker (Mode B) is a mock with a JSON file as its store. The gateway reaches it over loopback HTTP and proves itself with a key file, standing in for a Unix socket or pod-local restriction; that restriction itself is untested.

The front proxy is one nginx build with a minimal configuration, there to show that a component in front can refuse what the gateway accepts (P1-SS-04). Four cases go through it; the others address the gateway listener directly, on loopback, which is the only place it listens (P1-NL-01). Whether the eventual entry component behaves like this nginx has to be tested on that component.
Single gateway process: nothing here speaks to multi-replica behaviour, config rollout, quotas or load.

The read-back listener is exercised on this one instance with a publisher certificate made for the run; there is no publisher. Reading back from several replicas is tried in tests/integration/kubernetes.

The result holds for the agentgateway build named in this file only: the binary of the container image pinned in deploy/agentgateway/agentgateway.lock.json at the time of the run, taken out of the image and run on this host, not in a container. No other version or build is tested.
HTTP ExtAuthZ only. gRPC ExtAuthZ, decision caching, CONNECT, gRPC upstreams, HMAC signing and mTLS towards providers are untested.
DNS rebinding and network-layer egress ACLs are untested: the upstream is a fixed loopback address.
This is PoC evidence. It does not change any NOT_RUN acceptance case or STD-CP gate.
